stemMarkdown: A man travels from A to B at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 70 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds. Taking the one-way distance as $d$: time $= \dfrac{d}{60} + \dfrac{d}{70}$, so average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{d/60 + d/70} = \dfrac{2 \times 60 \times 70}{60 + 70} = 64.6154$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For equal distances the answer is the harmonic mean. The plain average $\dfrac{60 + 70}{2} = 65.0$ is the classic wrong answer, and it is always too high.
